hook: Every single one of the 28 lifts at Queen Mary Hospital failed.

sections.voiceover: Every single one of the 28 lifts at Queen Mary Hospital failed.
sections.visual_cue: Close-up of a static, out-of-order lift indicator at a hospital.
sections.sfx_cue: Mechanical clicking followed by a heavy digital silence.
b_roll: Exterior shot of the Queen Mary Hospital clinical block

sections.voiceover: On November 13, 2026, the Development Bureau submitted a 116-page report to the Legislative Council. What caused the lift shaft wall size and verticality deviations in this 34-storey clinical tower?
sections.visual_cue: A document page flip transition showing architectural diagrams.
sections.sfx_cue: Sound of paper rustling and turning.
b_roll: Close up of 116-page investigation report document
Wide shot of Legislative Council building

sections.voiceover: The report confirms these structural deviations spanned multiple contractors and various government departments in Hong Kong.
sections.visual_cue: Split screen showing multiple construction site errors in a grid.
b_roll: Graphics highlighting lift shaft verticality deviations

sections.voiceover: The investigation identified four main causes, including guide rail verticality deviations and unbalanced lift cars. Chief Executive John Lee ordered this probe after officials sealed off the 28 lifts in September.
sections.visual_cue: Animated diagram showing a tilted lift shaft versus a straight one.
b_roll: Diagram of unbalanced lift car centers
Empty hospital corridor with lift doors closed

sections.voiceover: All 28 lifts remain under scrutiny after these systemic errors.
sections.visual_cue: Wide shot of the Queen Mary Hospital clinical tower at dusk.
